corrections.source_says: The task-quality outcome also has an originality-only robustness analysis, which should be recorded in measure_detail under form-spec rule 7. The paper reports the cognitive-diversity-to-originality path as b = 4.619, SE = 1.346, p < 0.01, and the serial indirect pathway through negative socio-emotional interactions and cognitive diversity, relative to full AI access, as b = -0.105, SE = 0.050, 95% CI [-0.248, -0.036]. These are mediation-path estimates, not a direct comparison of arm means; the signs are reproduced as printed.
corrections.quote: To test the robustness of our findings, we re-ran the mediation analysis using originality as the sole indicator of task quality.
corrections.locator: PDF pp. 10-11, Section 4.4.2, Measuring task quality by originality; associated model caption on p. 12, Figure 6.

confirmed: Design class lab_rct and context_class none are supported: teams were randomly assigned to unequal or full GenAI access; the recipient within unequal-access teams was also randomly selected (PDF pp. 5-6, Sections 3 and 3.2).

The study reports 120 university students in 60 two-person teams; Table 3 gives 40 unequal-access teams and 20 full-access teams. The sample exceeds 50 people; no participant exclusions are reported, and separate arm-level people counts are not printed (PDF pp. 5-6, Sections 3-3.1; p. 8, Section 4; p. 11, Table 3).

All teams completed the no-AI task first, followed by the randomized AI configuration; the baseline reused the participants and used an electric-bicycle prompt, whereas treatment used AR glasses (PDF p. 6, Sections 3 and 3.2-3.3; p. 14, Section 5.4).
Kimi 3.0 was the named Moonshot model; permitted users could interact freely, the writing task was in Chinese, and each task was limited to 45 minutes (PDF p. 6, Sections 3.2-3.3).

Blinded marketing experts graded submissions from 1 to 7 on writing quality, content quality and originality. Nine raters evaluated 120 submissions, with three raters per submission; these submission and rater counts are distinct from the participant count (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 3.4.2.1).
The task-quality reported string and one-line finding match the PDF: unequal access M = 5.654, SD = 0.080; full access M = 5.250, SD = 0.118; t = 2.881, p < 0.01 (PDF p. 8, Section 4.1).
The cognitive-diversity reported string matches the PDF: unequal access M = 0.631, SD = 0.011; full access M = 0.510, SD = 0.018; t = 5.938, p < 0.01 (PDF pp. 8-9, Section 4.2).

Cognitive diversity is cosine distance between normalized Universal Sentence Encoder vectors of each teammate's concatenated spoken utterances. It compares teammates' discussion transcripts, not final press releases across teams (PDF p. 7, Section 3.4.3).

The form correctly preserves the source's SD labels while noting that Figure 4 defines its error bars as plus or minus one standard error of the mean (PDF pp. 8-9, Sections 4.1-4.2 and Figure 4 caption).

The document is the 16-page Frontiers in Psychology journal article by Jiaxuan Han and Ruqin Ren, published 8 September 2025. The complete markdown was read, and the form's numerical claims were checked against PDF pages (PDF p. 1 and document page count).

The external Table_1.DOCX supplement was independently retrieved through Europe PMC and read in memory. It contains writing-task instructions, task-quality scoring criteria, and Bales interaction-process categories with examples, with no additional effect estimates (PDF p. 14, Supplementary material; Table_1.DOCX, sections Writing Tasks, Task Quality Scoring Criteria, and Bales’ Interaction Process Analysis Categories with Examples).
This is one primary laboratory experiment, not a synthesis; the synthesis fields appropriately contain no pooled estimates (PDF pp. 5-12, Sections 3-4).
summary: The paper contains a randomized laboratory study of 120 students in 60 two-person teams and belongs in the two-screener pipeline. The reported counts, contrasts, and source description are supported, but the task-quality outcome omits the originality-only robustness analysis in Section 4.4.2.
